items.alt: Rocky coast on the southwest of Palaui Island

children.text: Off the coast of Santa Ana in Cagayan province, Palaui Island is a pristine island designated a marine protected area. Climb to Cape Engaño Lighthouse, built in
, for views over grassy hills and blue sea, and spend a slow day on quiet beaches and in village homestays.
Palaui Island is an island with a land area of about
24km²
lying off Santa Ana, Cagayan, at the northeastern tip of Luzon. It was designated a marine reserve (Palaui Island Marine Reserve) by presidential proclamation in
, and in
a law (Republic Act 11038) upgraded about
80km²

including the surrounding sea to a Protected Landscape and Seascape. Thanks to strict limits on development, there is not a single large resort, and grassy hills, primary forest, coral reefs, and quiet fishing villages remain almost as they were. The sea around the island holds healthy coral reefs and a variety of fish, making it ecologically important as well.
The island's symbol is Cape Engaño Lighthouse, standing on a hill about
above sea level at Cape Engaño on the northern tip. Construction of the stone lighthouse began in
, in the last years of Spanish colonial rule, and it was completed in
; it is the work of Magín Pers y Pers, who also designed the Cape Bojeador Lighthouse in Ilocos Norte and the Capones Island Lighthouse in Zambales. An octagonal tower about

high and the keepers' quarters and storehouses stand together inside a walled compound; the quarters are close to ruins, but the tower is fitted with solar-powered lights and is an active lighthouse maintained by the Philippine Coast Guard. The view from in front of the lighthouse is overwhelming. Green grassland flows down toward the sea, and below you turquoise water and small rock islets lie scattered, a scene that many say reminds them of Batanes.
Palaui became known around

after appearing as a filming location for a foreign survival reality show and being featured on international lists of beautiful beaches. Even so, it remains an island with limited electricity and communication, and travelers stay at homestays or campsites in the village of Punta Verde for a day close to unspoiled nature.
It suits travelers who want a remote, simple experience over convenient comfort, and those who enjoy trekking and camping. Since it takes about
3–4 hours
overland from the transport hub of Tuguegarao in northern Luzon, it's not easy to reach, so staying at least one night to combine the lighthouse trek with island hopping is recommended.
The island measures about
10km
long and
5km
wide, with a sheer rocky coast on the west and a coral reef extending about
2.4km

out to sea on the east. Two rock islets called Dos Hermanos lie off the northern cape. About 90 species of migratory birds visit the protected area, and the surrounding waters hold 21 commercial fish species and about
50ha
of coral reef. Tourism on the island has been run since

by the Palaui Environmental Protectors Association (PEPA), formed by residents, through guiding, a village kitchen, and souvenir making, and for this work it received the ASEAN Community-Based Tourism Award in
Land your boat on the island's north coast and climb about
20–30 minutes
up steps and a trail through grassy hills to the lighthouse. The view from the hill in front of it, over the coastline and rock islets, is the highlight of a Palaui trip.

blocks.title: Trek through the jungle from Punta Verde to the lighthouse

children.text: This walk starts from Punta Verde, a village on the south of the island, and takes you through forest and grassland to the lighthouse with a guide. The Lagunzad Trail is about
7km
and takes
2 hours 30 minutes–3 hours 30 minutes
, while the Leonardo Trail, which passes Baratubut Falls, is about
and takes
2–3 hours
. Beginners can manage it, but the shadeless grassland sections are long, so an early-morning start is best.

The village of Punta Verde has homestays run by residents. With electricity limited on the island, falling asleep to the sound of waves after a fish dinner cooked by your host is a unique part of this island's charm.
On the Santa Ana mainland side, Anguib Beach has fine white sand and calm turquoise water, and is often visited together with Palaui island hopping. It's good for swimming and snorkeling.
A small rocky islet near San Vicente port, named for its resemblance to a crocodile's shape. Its shallow sandbar and clear water make it a pleasant spot to rest and take photos.
Snorkeling with a guide in designated zones around the island reveals coral reefs and tropical fish. Since this is a protected area, never step on or touch the coral.

blocks.title: Sunrise and sunset from the lighthouse hill

children.text: If you camp or take an early boat, you can watch the Pacific sunrise from the lighthouse hill. The wind is strong, but dawn on this near-empty hill is something special.
This tiered waterfall, about
high, is a walk of about
30 minutes

along a forest path from Punta Verde village. It lies partway along the Leonardo Trail, so it combines well with the lighthouse trek, and you can cool off in the pool beneath the falls. A guide must accompany you.

On days when rough seas block landing on the northern shore near the lighthouse, you often switch to visiting only nearby Crocodile Island and Punta Verde, or landing at Punta Verde and walking a forest path to the lighthouse. Whether the boat goes out is decided at the port on the morning of the day.

Trekking trails are sometimes closed depending on how the protected area is being managed. When the island reopened after the pandemic in

, only the northwestern lighthouse area was open and trekking on the village side was suspended for a while, so check at the visitor center first which trails are open that day and where the boat will drop you off and pick you up.
Philippine Airlines and Cebu Pacific fly from Manila to Tuguegarao Airport (TUG), the capital of Cagayan province, a flight of about
1 hour
, with one-way fares of roughly
. From the airport to the downtown van terminal is about
10–15 minutes
by tricycle.
Vans to Santa Ana leave Tuguegarao city regularly, taking about
3–4 hours
and costing about
. From Manila, Victory Liner, GV Florida, and others run to Tuguegarao in about
11–12 hours
(about
), and some companies such as Florida run direct night buses from Sampaloc, Manila to Santa Ana (about
13–15 hours
). If coming from Pagudpud in Ilocos, it takes about
4–5 hours
along the coastal road via Claveria and Aparri.
A tricycle ride of
15–20 minutes

from Santa Ana town takes you to San Vicente port. At the port's tourism registration office, you register as a visitor and pay the fees, then charter a boat from the accredited boatmen's cooperative. It takes about
20–30 minutes
to reach Palaui Island and
45 minutes–1 hour
to reach the Cape Engaño shore. Boats are chartered per boat, with fares set by destination and time, so going with several people greatly reduces the cost per person.
GV Florida Transport runs a direct deluxe bus from its Sampaloc terminal in Manila to Santa Ana via Roxas in Isabela province twice a day (
and
). The trip takes about
14–16 hours

, arriving at the Florida terminal in Santa Ana town (the Centro) in the early morning or morning of the next day, so you can go straight to the port and catch the first boat. With only two departures a day, book ahead during Holy Week and long weekends, and check the company's announcements before you leave, as schedules can change.
From Manila to Santa Ana is about

. Exit the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) and head up to Tuguegarao along the Maharlika Highway (Pan-Philippine Highway), which passes through Nueva Ecija, Dalton Pass in Nueva Vizcaya, and Isabela; then continue north through Lal-lo and Gonzaga into Santa Ana. Driving time alone is around
10 hours
, so many people break the trip with a night in Tuguegarao or Isabela. From Tuguegarao to Santa Ana is about
148km

After registering and paying the fees at the Ecozone Visitor Center at the port, you are assigned a boat at the dispatch counter of the boatmen's association PASAMOBA. Bargaining separately with boatmen is prohibited.
Each boat carries up to 8 people, and if you exceed the set usage time (about
5 hours
), roughly
per hour is added.
The best time is from
March
to
May

. The sea is calm then, making boat travel safe, and clear skies bring out the sharpest views from the lighthouse hill. The grass can turn a bit yellow late in this period, but the sea color is at its most beautiful.
From
November
to
February
, the strong northeast monsoon brings high waves and frequent rain. Since Palaui faces the Pacific and Bashi Channel, boat trips are often canceled during this period.
From
June
to
October

is the rainy and typhoon season. Northeastern Cagayan province often lies in the path of typhoons coming up from the Pacific, so when a typhoon is forecast, the port suspends all sailings entirely. Early
June
can sometimes be manageable, but weather swings widely.
Santa Ana's annual rainfall is about 1,818mm, with the most rain in
October–December
(240–300mm per month) and the least in
April
(about 48mm). Daytime highs are a cool
in
January
and climb to about
in
April–June
. Santa Ana's Viray Festival is held every year on
, with street parades and cultural performances. The area lies in the path of strong typhoons: on
September 22, 2025
, Super Typhoon Nando (Ragasa) even made landfall at Calayan in the Babuyan Islands just to the north.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
There are no resorts on the island — only resident homestays and a designated campsite in Punta Verde village. Homestays cost about

per person per night, very affordable, but most have electricity only for a few evening hours or rely on solar power, and the bathroom and shower facilities are basic. For more comfort, you can stay at a guesthouse or resort in downtown Santa Ana or near San Vicente port (about
per night) and island-hop for the day instead. Anguib Beach also has cottage-style lodging and a camping area.

There are no restaurants on the island, so it's common to ask your homestay host to prepare a meal, or buy rice, fish, and drinks at the Santa Ana market and have them cooked for you. The waters off Santa Ana are rich in fish, so tuna, grilled fish, shellfish, and crab dishes are cheap and fresh. For Cagayan regional food, be sure to try Tuguegarao's famous pancit batil patong when passing through.

Santa Ana town (the Centro) has a cluster of small beachfront resorts and inns, making it convenient for catching the first boat at dawn. Some places with a pool and restaurant, such as the long-established Jotay Resort, start at about

per night. On the island, the residents' village kitchen sometimes serves meals made with local seafood and wild honey gathered on the island, so ask about meals when you register. True to its nickname, "Game Fishing Capital of the Philippines," Santa Ana has lively sea fishing and even holds a cutlassfish fishing tournament.
There are few ATMs in Santa Ana, and the island has no payment method besides cash. Withdraw plenty of cash in Tuguegarao.
Phone signal is weak or absent on the island. Let your family know your itinerary in advance and download offline maps beforehand.
A power bank and flashlight (headlamp) are essential. Homestay electricity is available for only a short time.
Start the lighthouse trek before
. There's no shade on the grassland stretch, and it gets very hot at midday.
Pack water, snacks, mosquito repellent, a towel, and a change of clothes in a waterproof bag. Boat spray can easily soak your gear.
Since boats are chartered per boat, joining other travelers at San Vicente port can significantly cut costs.
The campsite and homestays get busy during Holy Week and the
May
holidays. It's a good idea to contact the Santa Ana tourism office or a homestay in advance.

per person) and the guide fee (
for 1–4 people,
for 5–6 people) are paid only at the Ecozone Visitor Center at San Vicente port. You leave a separate
garbage deposit, which is returned when you come back and show the trash you took along.
From the Engaño Bay beach to the lighthouse, you climb about 200–300 steps and a dirt path for
20–30 minutes
. You often step into the water getting off the boat, so bring trekking sandals or water shoes that can get wet, and a hat.

Conditions such as that day's sailings, whether overnight stays on the island are allowed, and daily visitor limits change frequently. Check with the Santa Ana tourism office or the boatmen's association (PASAMOBA) before you leave.
Palaui Island is a marine protected area. Collecting coral, shells, or plants, littering, and illegal fishing are all prohibited. Bring back all the trash you bring in.
Visitor registration and a licensed guide are mandatory. Do not land by private boat without registering.
During the northeast monsoon and typhoon season, high waves cancel boat trips. If your boatman refuses to sail, don't push them to go anyway.
The old buildings around the lighthouse have deteriorated with age. Don't enter off-limits areas or climb on collapsed structures.
There are no medical facilities on the island. Bring a basic first-aid kit and antiseptic, and avoid strenuous hikes.
Typhoons don't come only in
June–October
. On
November 7, 2024
, Typhoon Marce (Yinxing) made landfall directly at Santa Ana. Before you leave, be sure to check the PAGASA typhoon forecast and the Coast Guard's sailing-ban announcements.
Palaui is an island that can only be preserved by accepting some inconvenience. Please be a guest who follows the island's rules rather than expecting full amenities.
